newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSTRALIAN Q3 WAGES - Review of forecasts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSTRALIAN Q3 WAGES - Review of forecasts.

text.p: Australian average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) data is due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Wages growth is expected to fall to the lowest level in two years, and following on from Wednesday's favourable CPI data, a moderation in wages would support calls for a rate cut.
The median forecast of the 31 economists Reuters surveyed was for a 1.0 percent rise, taking annual growth to 3.7 percent.
Quarterly forecasts ranged from rises of 0.7 to 3.4 percent, leading to annual forecasts between 3.4 and 4.0 percent.
Recent AWOTE data, and third quarter forecasts, are detailed below.

The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) called AWOTE "the most reliable guide to recent trends in wages growth," in its October Bulletin, but it also expressed concerns about future wages growth and growth in enterprise bargaining agreements

"While AWOTE is currently consistent with the two to three percent inflation objective, this reflects the modest growth in employment of the past year: the forward looking concern is that, with employment growing more strongly, AWOTE would once again be running at a pace which threatens price stability," the RBA said in the Bulletin, released last week.
However economists said a wages result in line with expectations or lower would make a rate cut more likely despite the RBA's concerns.
"... the wages issue is flagged as a risk, and a warning, it's not necessarily the most likely outcome," ANZ Treasury economists said in a commentary.

The fall in the consumer price index to a two year low of 2.1 percent in September, and likely further falls in coming quarters, should help cap wage claims, as would the continued softness in the labour market, economists said.

The fall in the underlying rate to 2.4 percent, although widely expected, and the expectation that it will remain in the two to three percent target band over at least the next year, should also ease RBA concerns, economists said.
With wages a key indicator of the future direction of the underlying rate, a low wages figure would fuel speculation about a near term rate cut on the basis of weak activity numbers.

"(The) wages data should add to the RBA's confidence that inflation will remain low -- particularly if AWOTE shows a rise of 1.0 percent or less in the September quarter," Macquarie Bank economists said.
